title: Research: RAC component composition/API patterns + domain component inventory
description: Final pre-build research. (A) External: react-aria-components composition & API best practices (compound components, slot/Provider context, polymorphism, controlled/uncontrolled, tv() variant exposure vs className, composeRenderProps conventions) — shapes how we structure our component APIs. (B) Internal: audit the soccer-manager's real + roadmapped screens and existing src/components/ui/* to inventory which primitives actually earn their place vs speculative. Feeds gf-4vk (palette) and gf-zun (substrate).
notes:
FINDINGS (2026-06-19). Two threads: (A) RAC composition/API patterns; (B) internal domain inventory.

== (A) COMPONENT API CONVENTIONS (adopt; our existing layer already encodes most) ==
1. Route EVERY RAC className through cx (= composeRenderProps + twMerge). Raw twMerge ONLY on plain DOM elements (Fieldset/Legend) — on a RAC primitive it stringifies a render-prop-function className and drops state styling.
2. Never shadow RAC state props (value/defaultValue/isSelected/isOpen/is*). Add only presentational tv() variants (intent/size), destructured out BEFORE spreading ...props.
3. Export tv() configs + their VariantProps (buttonStyles already exported) so consumers extend, not fork.
4. Style state with data-* / Tailwind variants in STATIC strings (pressed:, selected:, data-[focus-visible]:, in-disabled:) — current RAC+Tailwind recommendation. Use the render-prop FUNCTION form only to swap DOM/children by state (checkbox indicator Check-vs-Minus is the correct case).
5. ref as a plain prop (React 19), no forwardRef; type React.Ref<El>.
6. Preserve slot/id/data-slot/ref on every wrapped RAC child — that is the context wiring (Provider injects by type+slot; Label/Description/FieldError auto-wire aria-describedby). Note: RAC semantic slot prop != our data-slot styling hook; do not conflate.
7. Flat props (label='...') for the common single-control case; compound children only when interleaving custom nodes. Do NOT dot-namespace (Field.Label) what RAC context already composes — hurts tree-shaking; prefer named exports.
8. Subpath imports always (react-aria-components/Button) — never the barrel (kills tree-shaking). 'use client' ONLY where hooks/context/handlers live (button yes; pure-passthrough field.tsx no).
9. Polymorphism: RAC has NO asChild. Distinct primitives (Button vs Link) over a polymorphic 'as'. One RouterProvider wires all Link href routing; createLink only for bespoke link-likes.
Anti-patterns: twMerge(styles,className) on a RAC primitive; re-implementing controlled/uncontrolled over RAC value/onChange; inline className={({isHovered})=>...} where a data-hovered: variant works; barrel imports; forwardRef; thin passthroughs that add nothing (re-export instead).

== (B) DOMAIN INVENTORY ==
Real app surface is SMALL: squad (densest — sortable Table, career switcher, add-player modal, gating) + player-detail (stat cards, badges, DevelopmentChart) + account + auth. Domain-rich logic lives on squad + player-detail.

NO ui/* is dead weight. 'Zero app-usage' primitives (dialog/popover/dropdown/keyboard) are TRANSITIVE internals (modal->dialog; menu/select->dropdown+popover; dropdown->keyboard) — keep all. Lowest restyle value: keyboard, checkbox (1 marginal use in change-password), menu (theme-switcher only).

RESTYLE PRIORITY (by real-screen leverage): 1) Table (squad now; career-planning epic gf-498 is table-first across 498.1/498.2/498.5/498.6 — needs density modes, inline-edit, row status, filtering it does NOT have). 2) Button (everywhere, biggest visual payoff). 3) Card (squad/player/account/auth + coming finances summary cards). 4) Badge/status pill (status/tiers/pipeline — multiplies across career features). 5) Field/TextField/Input/NumberField/Select (every form + planning-field editor; NumberField domain-heavy: ratings/ages/fees). 6) Modal(+dialog). 7) line-chart/chart. 8) loader/toast/heading cheap. 9) menu/checkbox/keyboard lowest.

NET-NEW DOMAIN COMPONENTS we lack (career-planning epic gf-498, blocked on catalog importer gf-fwi.5, will hammer these):
- Data table w/ density + inline-edit + filtering + column status — current table is display+sort only. #1 gap; the epic is a spreadsheet replacement.
- Player/stat card (overall, position, value, status) — player-detail hand-rolls from Card+Badge; recurs across squad/shortlist/targets.
- Status/pipeline indicator (sign-status target->fee agreed->signed; squad status; action chips) — beyond flat Badge.
- Money/budget display + progress meter (Finances 498.3: currency fmt + spent/remaining/net bars) — nothing today.
- Filter/toolbar bar above tables (position/tier/status) — none exists.

IMPLICATION: restyle prioritizes button/card/field/table/badge; design data-table + stat-card + status-pipeline + money-meter + filter-bar as bespoke domain components NET-NEW alongside the token substrate.

title: Research foundation: design-system best practices + modern design principles
description: Before pinning palette (gf-4vk) and building the token substrate (gf-zun), establish a grounded foundation: (1) design-system architecture & token taxonomy best practices (primitive/semantic/component tiers, W3C Design Tokens spec, naming, theming); (2) what makes a design system EFFECTIVE + governance/sizing for a solo/small project (avoid enterprise over-engineering); (3) modern visual design principles (type scale, spacing, oklch color + accessible contrast, elevation, density, motion, current aesthetic). Output: a synthesized foundation doc + principles we adopt, recorded here. Feeds gf-4vk and gf-zun.
notes:
FOUNDATION SYNTHESIS (2026-06-19, 3 parallel research threads, primary-sourced: W3C DTCG, shadcn, Tailwind v4, MDN, EightShapes, Material, Evil Martians, WCAG 2.2, APCA). High convergence. Headline: we ALREADY own the load-bearing 20% — semantic oklch tokens (globals.css) + RAC behavior. Foundation work = restraint + concrete values, not new machinery.

== ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLES (adopt) ==
1. TWO tiers only: primitive (oklch, named by appearance) -> semantic (named by role). No component-token 3rd tier until a real divergence need appears (promote after ~3 reuses; mainly justified by multi-brand, which we do not have). shadcn proves 2 tiers themeable + dark-capable with ~27 tokens.
2. Components reference SEMANTIC tokens only — never primitives, never raw hex. This is the rule that makes refactors + theming safe.
3. Keep flat shadcn-shaped names (--primary/--primary-fg, surface+content pairing). On-trend and correct.
4. DERIVE interactive states with color-mix(in oklch, ...) — do NOT hand-enumerate the state grid (that is the explosion anti-pattern). color-mix is Baseline since May 2023, production-safe. Reserve hand-authored 50-950 scales ONLY for tokens needing pinned AA contrast.
5. Theme by overriding the SEMANTIC layer only under .dark/[data-theme]; primitives declared once. Multi-theme-ready for free. Avoid light-dark() (Chrome-123-gated) — keep .dark class override (portable).
6. CSS @theme + :root/.dark is the single source of truth. @theme inline for per-theme-reassigned tokens. No build pipeline.
7. ONE state vocabulary + one emphasis axis, used consistently (e.g. -hover/-active + -soft/-subtle). Mixing vocabularies is the real smell.
8. Anti-drift toolchain = ONE CI-gated lint rule banning arbitrary/hex colors (bg-[#...]). Verify which linter the repo runs (oxlint) and add there; plus color-no-hex on the css.

== SKIP (enterprise ceremony for a solo single-consumer codebase) ==
DTCG JSON + Style Dictionary / Tokens Studio (no Figma, no 2nd platform — nothing reads the JSON; keep names DTCG-shaped as a free hedge). Component-token tier. Full 50-950 scales for the whole palette. Storybook + visual-regression CI (use ONE dev-only gallery route instead — ~80% value, 5% cost, cannot drift). Semver/changelog of an internal pkg. Contribution RFCs/governance. Multi-brand theming (light/dark is the ceiling). Formal deprecation windows. Git is our versioning: rename a token, let the compiler list call sites, fix same week.

== EFFECTIVE-DS HABITS (solo dev) ==
Abstract on the 2nd-3rd copy, never the 1st. Let real screens (squad list, player detail, match flow) pull components into existence — do not build the kit up front. Document INTENT in-code (when to use danger vs danger-subtle) next to the variant. Cap the palette; treat every new token as a cost. Traps: token sprawl, premature abstraction (11-bool DataCard), over-theming, just-this-once inline arbitrary values.

== A11y AT TOKEN/VISUAL LAYER (RAC handles behavior; these stay ours) ==
Contrast: WCAG 2.2 AA floor (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large/UI) + APCA as readability check (body Lc>=75, UI>=15; APCA not legal yet — improve with it, do not replace AA). Verify *-fg and *-subtle-fg pairs in BOTH themes (warning + subtle variants are the risk). Focus (2.4.11/2.4.13): --ring must hit 3:1 vs adjacent, not clipped by overflow:hidden; RAC gives data-focus-visible, we supply the visible ring. Target size (2.5.8): 24px min — touch-target utility already covers (44px); apply to icon-only controls. Motion (2.3.3): gate tw-animate-css behind prefers-reduced-motion. Color-not-sole-signal (1.4.1): pair every status color with icon/text — critical for a stats-dense soccer UI.

== MODERN-CLEAN CONCRETE DEFAULTS (feeds gf-4vk palette) ==
The Linear/Vercel/shadcn 'clean' = disciplined systems, not minimalism.
- Type: one sans (Inter/Geist, variable). font-feature cv11; tnum:1 on ALL stats/tables (digits must not jitter). Ramp px: 12,14(body),16,18,20,24,30 (ratio ~1.2 — bigger ratios read as marketing). Hierarchy via WEIGHT 400/500/600, not size; avoid 700+. Line-height 1.5 body / 1.25 headings; heading tracking -0.01 to -0.02em; measure 60-75ch.
- Spacing: 4px base / 8px rhythm (Tailwind v4 default via --spacing). Cadence 8/16/24-32. Dashboard density: row pad 8-12 vertical, card 16-24, page gutter 24-32. Few values used consistently > many tuned.
- Neutral (oklch light): bg 1 0 0, surface 0.985, muted 0.97, border 0.92, muted-text 0.55, text 0.15. Faint hue tint chroma <=0.01 (warmer than sterile pure gray).
- Accent: ONE hue, chroma ~0.13-0.18, L 0.55-0.65; derive states by +/-0.05 L. Semantics at matched L: success ~145deg, warning ~85deg, danger ~25deg.
- Dark: do NOT invert. Lift surfaces with lightness (bg ~0.18, raised cards 0.21-0.24 = elevation is lighter not shadow); reduce accent/semantic chroma 10-20% so colors do not vibrate.
- Elevation: BORDERS over shadows — 1px hairline neutral separates cards/panels; shadows ONLY for floating transient layers (dropdown/popover/dialog), two stacked low-opacity layers. Dark mode leans on surface-lightness.
- Radius: 6-8px default (cards/inputs/buttons), 4px chips/badges, 10-12px large/modals, full on avatars/toggles. (12-32px trend numbers are neumorphism — too soft.) Consistency > exact value.
- Motion: 150-200ms micro / ~300ms larger, ease-out entrances, animate transform+opacity only, prefers-reduced-motion -> fade/instant.
- Reads DATED: heavy drop shadows, big radii everywhere, multi-color palettes, pure #fff/#000, bold-weight hierarchy, oversized type ratios in product UI.

These map onto Tailwind v4 @theme + RAC data-[hovered]/[pressed]/[focus-visible]; the +/-0.05-L oklch tiers ARE the hover/pressed surfaces.

(1) Add color-mix(in oklab, ...) derived state tiers per semantic color (-hover/-soft/-soft-fg/-soft-hover), replacing hand-authored *-subtle pairs. (2) Add @utility status-focused/status-disabled/status-pending helpers. (3) Promote layout tokens: --disabled-opacity, --border-width, 3 semantic shadow roles (surface/overlay/field); keep the single --radius knob + calc() scale. (4) Apply the palette values from the palette bead. Full color-mix formulas are spec'd in gf-20y notes.
close_reason: Token substrate finalized + reviewed on spike/ui-direction branch: color-mix-derived -hover/-soft tiers (primary + danger/success/warning), --primary-subtle/-subtle-fg now derived, layout tokens (--disabled-opacity, surface/overlay shadow roles), @utility status-focused/status-disabled, accent locked to AA-safe blue oklch(0.54 0.18 262) with --ring/--sidebar-ring tracking it. Review cycle fixed a contrast regression (white-on-primary back to 5.22:1 AA) + ring hue drift + a dead --border-width token. Verified: white-on-primary 5.22 both themes, soft-fg 7.5+, focus-ring >=3:1, typecheck+oxfmt clean, /login renders. Uncommitted, pending commit decision; component migration is gf-a26.

title: Spike: UI component & design-system direction (keep react-aria, change the look)
description: We use IntentUI-derived react-aria-components primitives in src/components/ui/*, but dislike IntentUI's default styling. gf-vfv (the two-input checkbox) also showed the vendored components have drifted from upstream IntentUI. Decide the direction for our component styling / design system before sinking more work into the current look. react-aria-components stays as the behavior/accessibility layer regardless — this is purely about the visual/token layer and how we source it.
design: Time-boxed exploration, NOT an app-wide migration. Deliverables: (1) inventory which src/components/ui/* primitives are actually used and by whom; (2) articulate concretely what's disliked about IntentUI's look (palette, inset-ring borders, radii, density, overall feel); (3) decision criteria — aesthetic fit, migration effort/churn, accessibility preserved (all candidates keep RAC), upstream-drift/maintenance risk, theming/token flexibility, dark-mode; (4) prototype ~1-2 primitives (e.g. button + checkbox + a card) in the leading candidate directions on a throwaway branch so the look is visible on REAL components in the browser; (5) a written recommendation + follow-up beads for the chosen path. Candidate directions: A) restyle-in-place — keep current component APIs, rewrite the Tailwind/token layer to our own look (lowest churn, fully bespoke); B) Jolly UI — adopt shadcn's aesthetic on RAC via the shadcn CLI (turnkey shadcn look, re-vendor + reconcile small API diffs); C) define our own design system/token set from scratch. Refs: react-aria docs (canonical RAC patterns), IntentUI current source, Jolly UI (jollyui.dev), zaichaopan/react-aria-components-tailwind-starter.
acceptance_criteria: A written recommendation scoring the candidate directions against the decision criteria; at least one primitive prototyped per leading candidate and viewable in the browser; follow-up beads filed for the chosen direction. No app-wide component migration performed in this spike (that's separate, post-decision work).
notes:
RECOMMENDATION (2026-06-19): BUILD OWN. Keep react-aria-components 1.19 as the behavior layer (confirmed over Base UI — RAC is more a11y/i18n-rigorous and we have a working set). No project ships our target (RAC 1.19 + Tailwind v4 + tailwind-variants + derived per-component tokens + clean shadcn look), so vendor our own layer and steal patterns.

WHY NOT ADOPT: JollyUI = stale (last push Jan 2025, pins RAC 1.6), CVA, flat tokens. HeroUI v3 = RAC + best token system but a non-ownable npm package, playful look. COSS UI = Base UI not RAC (wrong primitive lineage; it is Cal.com's). shadcn v4 = Radix + flat oklch tokens (the baseline we are outgrowing). Park UI = ark-ui, Panda-first.

REFERENCES TO STEAL FROM (verified source):
- Token tiers: HeroUI v3 (ref dd674ae, MIT). color-mix() derived states instead of hand-authored scales.
- Token STRUCTURE: Park UI (layered semantic) — structure only, not code.
- RAC patterns: zaichaopan starter + our current IntentUI base.
- Clean neutral aesthetic: COSS/shadcn v4.

WHAT WE ALREADY HAVE (substrate is good): shadcn-shaped oklch tokens via @theme inline; tv() styling; per-component CSS-var hooks (button.tsx --btn-bg already does color-mix inline); composeRenderProps RAC wiring. The dislike is the LOOK (palette, inset-ring borders, radii/density), not the architecture.

SPEC — adopt at two levels, keeping our tv() idiom and shadcn token NAMES (rename HeroUI accent/muted/surface back to avoid collision):

LEVEL 1 (substrate, ~zero call-site churn) in globals.css:
1. color-mix() derived state tiers per semantic color:
   --primary-hover: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 90%, var(--primary-fg) 10%);
   --primary-soft: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 15%, transparent);
   --primary-soft-fg: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 70%, var(--fg) 30%);
   --primary-soft-hover: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 20%, transparent);
   (same shape for danger/success/warning/secondary; replaces hand-authored *-subtle pairs)
2. @utility status-* helpers (focus ring, disabled, pending) applied across components instead of re-spelling:
   status-disabled => opacity:var(--disabled-opacity); cursor:not-allowed; pointer-events:none
3. Layout tokens promoted to first-class: --disabled-opacity, --border-width, 3 semantic shadow roles (surface/overlay/field) rather than t-shirt scale. Keep existing single --radius knob + calc() scale.
4. Clean palette retune (light+dark oklch): neutral base, subtle 1px borders replacing IntentUI inset-ring, moderate radii.

LEVEL 2 (opportunistic, mechanical churn): standardize the per-component local-var indirection (base wires layout+state once; variants reassign --x-bg only) across all ui/* (button already does it; bring checkbox/input/etc in line).

NOT TAKING: HeroUI v3 per-component BEM .css files (tv()->prop->class map) — keeps styling in tv() strings, splitting a component across .tsx+.css is a maintainability tradeoff we are not adopting just to match their internal org. CVA. 50-900 scales. npm-package model.

DEFERRED: browser prototype (button+checkbox+card on new substrate) — user de-scoped for now; filed as follow-up, it is the validation gate BEFORE any app-wide migration.
close_reason: Spike complete. Decision: BUILD-OWN component layer on react-aria-components (researched JollyUI/HeroUI v3/COSS/Base UI/Park UI/shadcn v4 — none fit). Deliverables met: scored written recommendation (bead notes), prototype viewed in browser (gf-w5q), foundation+composition+inventory research (gf-6ww, gf-dme), accent locked to AA-safe blue oklch(0.54 0.18 262), token substrate built+reviewed+committed (gf-zun, 1cff78d). Follow-up filed: gf-a26 (component migration, post-spike). No app-wide migration done in the spike, as scoped.

title: Harden email verify link against scanner/preview prefetch (single-use GET token)
description:
The /api/auth/verify-email link is a single-use GET token. Corporate email security (Microsoft Defender for O365, Proofpoint, Mimecast) and inbox preview bots PREFETCH links, consuming the token before the human clicks. With autoSignInAfterVerification on, the scanner's GET verifies the email (and gets a discarded session); the real user then clicks a dead token, hits an error page, and never lands on /squad?verified=1 — so the gf-2hf confirmation toast never fires. This hits exactly the corporate/self-hosted environments the platform migration (gf-fwi) targets.

The user is actually verified (the prefetch did it), but the UX is a dead-link error instead of a success landing.

Community-recommended mitigations (pick one):
- POST-confirm landing page: the email link lands on an app page with a 'Confirm' button that POSTs to verify — defeats prefetch cleanly (one extra click).
- Refuse to consume the token on HEAD requests.
- Detect known scanner user-agents and 200 without consuming.
- Put the token in the URL fragment of an intermediate page (fragments aren't fetched by scanners).

Refs: better-auth Discussion #6985 (magic-link token consumed by scanners), Supabase #41618, PocketBase #7102. Better Auth's magic-link plugin exposes allowedAttempts for this; core email-verification may not, so an app-level confirm page is likely the path.

Pre-existing (not introduced by gf-cpq/gf-2hf) but undermines verification reliability + the toast.
design: Prefer the POST-confirm landing page (most robust, defeats prefetch). Coordinate with gf-2hf: the confirm page can be where ?verified=1 / the toast originates instead of relying on the raw verify redirect surviving a scanner. Relates to gf-fwi.16 (auth hardening for prod/reverse-proxy).

title: Relocate auth into src/modules/auth and dedupe the auth forms
description:
Decision: ADR 0015 (docs/decisions/0015-auth-as-feature-module.md). Collapse all auth code into one feature module, retire src/lib/auth, then dedupe the four _auth route forms behind shared primitives.

STAGE A — relocate (behavior-identical, its own commit):
- Move src/lib/auth into src/modules/auth: lib/server.ts (keep server-only marker), lib/client.ts (add client-only marker), lib/sanitize-redirect.ts (+ test), lib/invite-store.ts. functions.ts becomes api/get-session.ts (static import of the marked server; isomorphic RPC boundary, NOT marked).
- Schemas split per-form under modules/auth/schemas/: login.ts, sign-up.ts, forgot-password.ts, reset-password.ts + a shared fields.ts (reused email/password/invite/name validators). NOT a single root schemas.ts. messages.ts stays at the module root.
- Extract use-sign-out into modules/auth/hooks/use-sign-out.ts; SignOutButton becomes a thin consumer (button relocation into the header is gf-t5m).
- Split errors.ts: auth copy to modules/auth/messages.ts; the generic UNEXPECTED_ERROR_MESSAGE to src/lib/messages.ts.
- Move the auth integration tests (invite-gate, session, password-reset, email-flows) with their files, keeping the .integration.ts naming.
- Repoint the ~11 import sites (root-error + its test, sign-out-button + its test, the four _auth routes, _app/route, _public/index, routes/api/auth/$.ts) to #/modules/auth/*.
- Drop the old functions.ts entry from the eslint dynamic-import exempt list (get-session is static).
- Update the architecture.md Feature modules section into the module playbook (see this bead's notes).

The auth pgTable definitions do NOT move — they stay central in src/db/schema.ts for the single drizzle({schema}) import; modules/auth/lib/server.ts imports them from #/db/schema. See ADR 0015 Consequences.

STAGE B — dedupe the forms (the deepening; depends on Stage A):
- modules/auth/hooks/use-auth-submit.ts owns the error taxonomy: try/catch + logError + NETWORK_ERROR_MESSAGE on throw; 429 to RATE_LIMITED_MESSAGE; per-page result-error mapping to form/field; enumerationSafe flag for forgot-password (non-429 errors treated as success).
- modules/auth/components/auth-card.tsx (Card + form method=post + fields slot + FormError + submit) and auth-links.tsx.
- Convert login/sign-up/forgot/reset to thin per-page components composing useAppForm + AuthCard + use-auth-submit; route files become shells with a local Page wiring route-typed context to plain props. Distinct per-page components, NOT one generic AuthForm, so forgot's success card and reset's no-token card stay local.
- Each page green as it lands.

CROSS-REF gf-fwi.17: it owns the static-import + server-only/client-only marker discipline and enumerates lib/auth/{server,client}.ts by path. After this move those become modules/auth/lib/{server,client}.ts and client.ts gains its client-only marker (advancing gf-fwi.17 Part A). api/get-session.ts is the isomorphic boundary (already static, not marked). gf-fwi.17 depends on this bead.

FOLLOW-UPS: auth email templates -> modules/auth/emails (gf-fwi.19); sign-out button into the header (gf-t5m); career/player forms -> TanStack Form (gf-fwi.20).
acceptance_criteria: ADR 0015 accepted; lib/auth removed; all consumers repointed to #/modules/auth; the four auth forms share useAuthSubmit + AuthCard; typecheck/lint/unit/integration/e2e/build + client-bundle leak grep all green.
notes:
Stage A architecture.md edit expands into the module playbook (folded in from the module-guidelines discussion, 2026-06-18). The "Feature modules" section gains:
1. Extend-vs-new-module decision rule: NEW module for a new domain entity with its own schema + lifecycle (e.g. future seasons / transfers / finances from the ideas docs); EXTEND a module for a new operation/view on an existing entity (server fn / hook / component into that module's api, hooks, components); a tightly-coupled sub-domain (e.g. player snapshots) stays a file/folder inside the parent module, not a new top-level module; anything used by 2+ modules goes to src/lib (infra) or src/components/ui (shared UI), never a module.
2. The lib-vs-modules boundary: feature code incl. auth lives in modules; lib is cross-cutting infra only (ADR 0015).
3. Record fc-2026's deliberate divergences from the finance-tracker reference so they are not later "fixed": central src/db + per-module schemas (not per-module db/), Zod (not ArkType), #/ alias (not @/).
The api/ thin-handler + static-import discipline stays owned by gf-fwi.17; reference it rather than restating.
CORRECTION (schema layout decided 2026-06-18): auth form schemas go in modules/auth/schemas/auth.ts, NOT a root schemas.ts. fc-2026 keeps the per-module schemas/ directory convention (career/player/catalog stay schemas/<entity>.ts, untouched). messages.ts stays at the module root. No schema-flatten work; existing modules are not restructured. Playbook line: module schemas live in a per-module schemas/ dir (one file per entity); promote nothing — flattening was considered and rejected for minimal-churn + room-to-grow.
SCHEMA GRANULARITY (clarified 2026-06-18): not one schemas.ts per module — individual files in schemas/, one per schema, named for what they validate, so the filename is the schema (findability; no opening a bundled file to see what's inside). Auth: schemas/login.ts, sign-up.ts, forgot-password.ts, reset-password.ts + a shared schemas/fields.ts (reused email/password/invite/name validators). This mirrors the per-page route shells and components (login.tsx route / login-form.tsx component / schemas/login.ts). Playbook line: schemas live in a per-module schemas/ dir, one descriptively-named file per schema. Existing modules (career/player/catalog) may be split per-schema as optional later cleanup, not required by this bead.
DRIZZLE-VS-ZOD SCHEMA DISTINCTION (2026-06-18) — keep separate in the playbook:
(1) Zod validation schemas: per-module schemas/ dir, one file per schema (split freely for findability).
(2) Drizzle table schemas (pgTable): must stay a single aggregated object for drizzle(client,{schema}); fc-2026 keeps ALL tables central in src/db/schema.ts and src/db/client.ts already does drizzle({casing,schema}) against it. The auth move relocates feature code only, NOT the pgTable definitions — auth tables (user/session/account/verification/invitation/invite_pending) stay in src/db/schema.ts; modules/auth/lib/server.ts imports them from #/db/schema (modules->db, correct direction). Single drizzle import preserved. architecture.md playbook must state this Zod-vs-Drizzle distinction explicitly.
STAGE A IMPLEMENTATION FINDING (2026-06-18): client.ts is NOT client-only marked. authClient is imported by SignOutButton, which is SSR-rendered in the root header, so client.ts is reached from server code and TanStack import-protection rejects a client-only marker at build (verified: build fails with it, passes without). authClient is isomorphic; client.ts stays unmarked. server.ts keeps server-only; api/get-session.ts is the unmarked isomorphic boundary. ADR 0015 corrected. Stage A gates all green: typecheck, lint 0, unit 139, integration 68, build, client-bundle leak scan (server tokens + secret absent).
STAGE A REVIEW CLARIFICATIONS (2026-06-18): (1) fields.ts holds only the genuinely reused validators (email, password). invite and name are sign-up-only, so they stay inline in schemas/sign-up.ts — nothing to share with; ADR 0015 corrected to match. (2) The "drop the old functions.ts entry from the eslint dynamic-import exempt list" step was moot: functions.ts was never on the exempt list (it already used static imports). get-session.ts is static, harmlessly covered by the existing src/modules/*/api/*.ts glob; tightening that glob is gf-fwi.17's territory. (3) architecture.md gained the deliberate-divergences-from-finance note (playbook item 3). Stage A review: codex + code-reviewer + pr-test-analyzer + silent-failure-hunter all clean; maintainability + spec-conformance report-only (no behavior issues). Added invalidate-not-called assertions to the sign-out failure-path tests.
close_reason: Auth is now a feature module (Stage A) with deduped forms (Stage B). Stage A (43730f6): relocated src/lib/auth -> src/modules/auth (lib singletons, api/get-session, per-form schemas/, messages, use-sign-out hook), retired lib/auth, repointed ~11 consumers. Stage B: extracted useAuthSubmit (429/network/per-page-code error taxonomy on a single discriminated AuthSubmitErrors union; folded the duplicate SignUpFormError) + AuthCard/AuthLinks; the four _auth forms are distinct per-page components behind thin route shells wiring route-typed context into router-agnostic forms (forgot's success card + reset's no-token card stay local); the curated-copy invariant lives in one tested hook. Reviewed across 3 cycles (codex + code-reviewer + pr-test + silent-failure + type-design + maintainability + spec-conformance), all clean; gates green: typecheck/lint/unit 144/integration 68/e2e 8/build/leak. One refinement: a rate-limited sign-up now shows the rate-limit message. Unblocks gf-fwi.17/.19/.20/gf-4m1/gf-t5m.

title: Sign-out / logout control for the gated app
description: gf-fwi.2.6 Stage 3' flipped the app behind a login gate (_app beforeLoad redirects to /login), but shipped no way to sign out — grep confirms zero signOut usage in src/. With the gate live, a manager has no UI to end their session or switch accounts, and the plan's own manual-verification step ('sign out -> /login') has no path. Add a sign-out control in the app shell/header that calls authClient.signOut(), then router.invalidate() so the _app guard re-runs against the now-empty session and redirects to /login (mirrors login.tsx's invalidate-before-navigate). Follow-up to gf-fwi.2.6.
acceptance_criteria: A visible sign-out control exists within the gated app; clicking it clears the session (authClient.signOut) and lands on /login; after sign-out, navigating to a gated route redirects to /login; an e2e covers sign-in -> sign-out -> gated route redirects.
notes: Originated as the one untracked gap from gf-fwi.2.6 Stage 3'-a review (gating without logout). Pairs with gf-vy9 for error feedback on a failed signOut. No app shell/header exists yet — the squad page renders its own <main>; placement (shared layout in _app/route.tsx component vs per-page) is an open design choice.
close_reason: Sign-out control added: header SignOutButton gated to the _app subtree; signs out, invalidates the router, returns to /login. e2e drives the real control. Failed-sign-out feedback deferred to gf-vy9.

title: Harden first-admin bootstrap against the concurrent-signup race
description: The first-user→admin bootstrap (src/lib/auth/server.ts createAuth) is a TOCTOU race: on a brand-new DB, two concurrent signups can both read hasUsers()===false before either commits, so both bypass the invite gate AND both get role='admin'. Accepted for now per decision 0013 (the gate is intentionally off for the first signup) and realistically unreachable for a single-operator self-host that signs up once right after deploy. Flagged by codex (P1) + review agents during gf-fwi.2.3. Fully closing it is architectural: the gate (plugin before-hook) and the admin-grant (better-auth user.create hook) live in separate hooks/requests, so a robust fix needs an out-of-band bootstrap (env-designated admin / one-time setup token) or a schema-backed single-winner (sentinel row + advisory lock). Address before exposing open/public registration.
design: FIX (env-designated admin, chosen 2026-06-17): INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL designates the bootstrap admin. createAuth(db, {initialAdminEmail?}) — defaults to env, overridable for tests. user.create.before: if adminExists() return; else require newUser.email===designated (lowercased) and grant role=admin, else throw APIError('FORBIDDEN',{code:'INVITE_REQUIRED'}). Gate enabled:adminExists (open only until first admin). DOUBLE-ADMIN RACE CLOSED: better-auth lowercases email pre-insert (sign-up.mjs:164) + UNIQUE email column = single-winner; two concurrent designated signups -> second insert fails -> one admin, no case-variant escape. Non-designated signups during bootstrap rejected with the same INVITE_REQUIRED surface as the closed gate (no bootstrap-state leak). RESIDUAL (accepted, inherent to open-gate model; Direction 2 seed+always-on-gate would eliminate): a sub-ms window where a NON-admin could pass the open gate then have adminExists flip true mid-flight -> created as a regular un-invited user. No privilege escalation. Fail-closed when INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL unset: every signup rejected until designated. Tests: invite-gate.integration (bootstrap, case-insensitive match, non-designated reject, gate-close, undesignated fail-closed); session/email-flows/password-reset integration + e2e webServer wired with INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL=manager.
notes: Source: gf-fwi.2.3 review. See the documented window in src/lib/auth/server.ts databaseHooks.user.create.before.
close_reason: Hardened first-admin bootstrap against the concurrent-signup TOCTOU race via env-designated admin (INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL). Only the designated email may register on a fresh DB and becomes admin; better-auth lowercases email pre-insert + the UNIQUE email column is the single-winner guard, so concurrent designated signups can't both claim admin (double-admin race CLOSED). Non-designated signups during the bootstrap window are rejected with the same INVITE_REQUIRED surface as the closed gate (no bootstrap-state leak); unset INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL fails closed. Gate enabled:adminExists (open only until first admin). Accepted residual (user chose env-designated over seed+always-on-gate): a sub-ms non-privileged gate-bypass window. Verified: 33 auth integration tests (incl. concurrent-winner, case-insensitive both sides, reopen-on-removal, fail-closed-undesignated) + 8 e2e (env->gate path end-to-end). Docs 0009/0013/spec-0001 updated. Follow-up gf-utf: constrain role column / 'admin' magic string.

title: Server-fn/request error-logging middleware (observability baseline)
description: gf-fwi.10 added the pino logger, but nothing logs server-fn/request errors yet: a thrown server function leaves no structured, contextual log line (only Nitro's default stderr). Add the minimal global request middleware that catches errors from Start-handled requests (serverFn + router), logs them via the logger with request context, and rethrows. This is the production observability baseline — do not deploy to prod without server-error logging. NOT the full wide-events model (gf-fwi.12 extends this).
design: Add the Start instance (no src/start.ts yet) and register a global request middleware via createStart({ requestMiddleware: [errorLog] }). errorLog = createMiddleware({type:'request'}).server(async ({ request, pathname, next, handlerType, serverFnMeta }) => try { return await next() } catch (err) { logger.error({ err, method, pathname, handlerType, fn: serverFnMeta?.name }, 'request error'); throw err }). Uses pino's {err} serializer (captures error.code). This is the SAME middleware gf-fwi.12 extends into wide-events (ALS field accumulation + one canonical log line per request + reqId from cf-ray) — foundation here, ambitious layer there. Refs installed @tanstack/start-client-core 1.170 createMiddleware (request type; handlerType serverFn|router; registered via createStart requestMiddleware).
close_reason: Error-logging request middleware delivered: src/start.ts (Start instance + global errorLogger request middleware logging THROWN server-fn/router errors via dynamically-imported pino then rethrow; CSRF re-added since defining start.ts disables Start's auto server-fn CSRF). handle-request-error.ts (log-and-rethrow helper, logger injected for client-safety) + is-loggable-error.ts (skips redirect/notFound control flow + sub-5xx Responses), both unit-tested. 5xx-Response-RESULT logging deferred to gf-fwi.12 (owns it, trigger note added). Reviewed 2 iterations (codex + 5 agents, all converged); 58 tests + typecheck/lint/build green; client bundle verified pino-free.

title: Migrate ui/* components to derived token substrate + standardize local-var convention (Level 2)
description: After prototype sign-off: point all src/components/ui/* at the new derived tokens and @utility status-* helpers, and standardize the per-component local-var indirection (base wires layout+state once; variants reassign --x-bg only) — button.tsx already follows this; bring checkbox/input/select/etc in line. Mechanical churn. NOT adopting HeroUI's per-component .css split; styling stays in tv() strings.
notes:
STATUS (2026-06-20): var(--color-X) -> raw var(--X) conversion DONE (fixes dark-mode color freeze) across button/badge/toast/checkbox/table/development-chart + the status-focused utility. ROOT CAUSE: CSS custom props inherit their COMPUTED value; a token defined '--color-fg: var(--fg)' is substituted at :root (light) and the frozen value inherits down — a .dark element cannot retroactively change it (true inline AND non-inline). @theme inline must stay: it makes UTILITIES inline to raw var(--fg) (re-resolve correctly); only ARBITRARY var(--color-*) reads were frozen. FIX = use raw tokens in arbitrary properties (re-resolve per element); kept utility classes + Tailwind builtins var(--color-white)/var(--color-sky-500). VERIFIED: button border re-resolves light vs dark (border_changed=true), 182 unit tests + typecheck + oxlint pass, dark /login renders correctly.

REMAINING (Level 2, deferred per user 2026-06-20): (a) adopt the derived --primary-hover/-soft tiers in component hover/soft states; (b) standardize the per-component local-var indirection (base wires layout+state once, variants reassign --x-bg only) across checkbox/input/select/etc; (c) apply @utility status-focused/status-disabled instead of re-spelling focus/disabled. Enhancement/refactor, not a bug.

title: e2e: real-delivery email verification lane (Mailpit) for full-suite runs
description: gf-cqi's e2e mints the verification JWT client-side (shared BETTER_AUTH_SECRET) and drives the real /api/auth/verify-email endpoint — fast, infra-free, and faithful to the verify→redirect round-trip, but it does NOT exercise the real email send. The 'is the emitted link correct' question is currently covered only at the integration layer (email-verification.integration.ts asserts the SENT URL) — nothing asserts the full SMTP→template→clickable-link chain end-to-end in a browser. Add an opt-in real-delivery e2e lane that captures the actual email and clicks the actual link, for full-suite confidence in the production email path (template, encoding, callbackURL sharp edges #5015/#3812).
design: Keep the minted-token path (gf-cqi) as the fast default for every run; this is a SEPARATE opt-in lane, not a replacement. Integration point: the e2e harness is testcontainers-based (global-setup spins up @testcontainers/postgresql), NOT docker-compose. RECOMMENDED: add a Mailpit testcontainer in global-setup mirroring the Postgres one (Mailpit: SMTP :1025, HTTP API :8025), and wire SMTP_URL + EMAIL_FROM into playwright.config webServer.env exactly like DATABASE_URL — planEmailTransport already routes to SMTP when SMTP_URL is set (smtpUrl wins over CF token). Test flow: sign up the invitee → poll Mailpit's /api/v1/messages for the message → extract the verify link from the body → page.goto(link) → assert the same banner-clears + form-unlocks outcome gf-cqi asserts via the minted token. ALTERNATIVE: a long-lived Mailpit in a docker-compose shared by dev + e2e — only worth it if dev also wants a local mailbox; otherwise the testcontainer is less machinery. Gate this lane to full-suite/CI (e.g. a @mail tag or project) so it doesn't slow per-PR runs.
acceptance_criteria: A tagged/opt-in e2e test signs up an unverified invitee, captures the real verification email via Mailpit, extracts and navigates the actual link, and asserts the banner clears + the real create-career form unlocks (same outcome as gf-cqi). SMTP_URL+EMAIL_FROM wired into webServer.env; Mailpit started by the harness (testcontainer or compose). The default minted-token lane (gf-cqi) is unchanged and still runs on every invocation.

title: Dev seed script for a known local admin (db:seed)
description:
Verifying any signed-in feature in local dev needs an authenticated session, but the dev admin (admin@example.com) had no known password — forcing a password reset (mutating dev data) each time. Make local dev-admin access reproducible.

Add an idempotent 'pnpm db:seed' that ensures a known local admin exists:
- email admin@example.com, role admin, email_verified=true, password 'password123' (the same convention the integration tests already use).
- Idempotent: safe to re-run; upserts rather than duplicating. Use Better Auth's own password hashing (auth.api / signup path or the password util) so the hash is valid — do NOT hand-roll a scrypt hash.
- Run after 'pnpm db:dev:reset' to get a clean, signed-in-able dev DB in one command.

Document the credential (admin@example.com / password123) in AGENTS.md (or docs/dev.md) — it's a local-only throwaway account, so committing it is fine, not a secret.

Bonus: this is the foundation for an e2e auth fixture (Playwright storageState) — coordinate with gf-cqi and gf-fwi.9 (e2e POM/fixtures) so the seeded admin / sign-in helper is shared rather than duplicated.

Discovered during gf-4wj browser verification (had to reset the admin password to sign in).
design: Idempotent seed using Better Auth's hashing (not a raw DB hash). Wire as a package.json script. Document creds in AGENTS.md. Relates to gf-cqi / gf-fwi.9 (e2e fixtures).

title: Checkbox renders two nested <input type=checkbox> for a string child
description:
src/components/ui/checkbox.tsx wraps children in react-aria's <CheckboxButton>, and for a STRING child it renders <CheckboxLabel> — which is ANOTHER <CheckboxButton>. Each CheckboxButton emits its own visually-hidden <input type=checkbox>, so a string-child Checkbox produces TWO checkbox inputs for one logical control. The OUTER input carries no visible label text (only the inner control-label has 'Sign out other devices').

Surfaced by the gf-4wj /account 'Sign out other devices' checkbox (the first/only consumer passing a string child). Verified in the browser: the rendered DOM has two <input type=checkbox>; both track the same CheckboxField state (a real click toggles both), so it FUNCTIONS correctly. accesslint/axe-core reports NO WCAG violation. But it's a semantic redundancy, and the unlabeled outer checkbox is a latent screen-reader concern (an SR navigating by form controls may encounter a second, unnamed checkbox).

Fix: in checkbox.tsx, don't wrap a string child in a second CheckboxButton — render the label text inside the existing CheckboxButton (e.g. a plain <span data-slot=control-label> instead of CheckboxLabel/CheckboxButton), so only one input is emitted. Verify with the /account page (re-run the accesslint + DOM check) and any other Checkbox consumers.
design: Pre-existing shared-component defect, low severity (functional + no axe violation). Touch only checkbox.tsx; re-verify /account renders one input and the change-password 'sign out other devices' value still flows. Discovered during gf-4wj browser verification.
close_reason: String child now renders one named input via a plain <span data-slot=control-label> inside the single CheckboxButton, instead of a second CheckboxButton (CheckboxLabel) that emitted its own hidden input. Removed the now-unused CheckboxLabel export. Matches react-aria docs + current IntentUI patterns. Browser-verified on /account (one input, correct name, toggles, accesslint clean); added colocated regression + toggle tests (user-event).

title: User profile/settings page (change email, password, account)
description:
A dedicated signed-in profile/settings surface that hosts account-management actions, discoverable from the app header (signed-in only). Replaces the idea of bolting change-email onto the verification banner.

Scope (incremental):
- Change email: surface the gf-3aw escape hatch here. Backend is DONE (Better Auth user.changeEmail.enabled + updateEmailWithoutVerification, session-guard before-hook on /change-email that rejects verified accounts, integration tests). This bead owns the UI: an inline change-email form (TanStack Form + useAuthSubmit + a change-email schema/message), shown only while the session is unverified; refetch the session on success so the verification banner reflects the new address.
- Password change for signed-in users: ties to gf-3x4 (authenticated password-change with 'sign out other devices').
- Future: a verified-account email-change flow (confirm via the OLD address via sendChangeEmailConfirmation) so the /change-email guard can be relaxed for verified users.

Design notes:
- New route src/routes/_app/account.tsx under the auth-gated _app layout.
- Header link (signed-in only) near SignOutButton in __root.tsx.
- Email-change verification links already redirect to /squad?verified=1 (gf-2hf), so the toast fires on the new address too.
design: Change-email backend already landed under gf-3aw (server.ts + email-verification.integration.ts). This bead is UI-first: account route, header entry, inline change-email form gated to unverified sessions. Keep password-change coordinated with gf-3x4.
notes: Owns the FULL change-email feature (backend + UI). The backend prototype was reverted during review: naively enabling Better Auth user.changeEmail (updateEmailWithoutVerification) bypasses email-bound invites for unverified invitees. Design must address: (a) does change-email even apply under email-bound invites? the typo-at-signup case is unreachable since signup enforces EMAIL_MISMATCH; (b) verified-account change needs old-address confirmation (sendChangeEmailConfirmation); (c) if kept, re-bind/re-validate against the invite. See bd memory betterauth-hooks-and-changeemail.
close_reason: Shipped the /account settings page: header link (signed-in only), change-password (gf-3x4), and verified-only change-email via Better Auth two-step old-address confirmation. NB the bead's original DESIGN/Scope lines were superseded — change-email is verified-only (not unverified), the backend landed here (not gf-3aw), and there's no session refetch (the change is deferred to the new address's confirmation). Browser-verified end-to-end.

title: e2e: unverified-user verification banner + feature gating flow
description:
gf-7mm's progressive-verification UX (dismissable banner, request-link + cooldown, and the gated create-career/add-player/record-snapshot buttons) is covered only by component tests. The e2e suite exercises just the auto-verified bootstrap admin, who never sees any of it. Add a browser e2e for the unverified path.

Needs a new harness: an invited-unverified-user (the existing FIRST_MANAGER is the bootstrap admin → auto-verified). Steps: bootstrap the admin, create an invitation (DB insert or admin flow), sign up an invitee with the code → they land signed-in but emailVerified:false. Then assert: the verification banner renders (role=status, shows the email); the squad write triggers render as aria-disabled GatedActionButtons (not the real modals) and toast on activate; the create-career empty-state shows the gated 'Create career' button; (optionally) resend hits the cooldown. Verifying the email (read the verification token from the DB like latestResetToken does for resets, hit the verify endpoint) should clear the banner and unlock the real controls.

The invited-unverified-user harness this builds is reusable for other invited-flow e2e. Relates to gf-fwi.9 (shared Playwright POM/fixtures). Discovered during gf-7mm review (no e2e for the unverified path).
notes: Beyond the banner/gating coverage: this e2e must verify the ?verified=1 round-trip survives Better Auth's verify-email → redirect end-to-end (read the verification token from the DB like the reset tests do, hit /api/auth/verify-email, assert the browser lands on /squad?verified=1 and the 'Email verified' toast fires once). Reason: callbackURL-with-query-param has known Better Auth sharp edges (#5015 encoding, #3812 double-decode) — our integration test only checks the SENT email URL, not the redirect. This is the only thing that locks gf-2hf end-to-end. Note: gf-0bo (scanner prefetch) may change the verify flow to a POST-confirm page; coordinate so this e2e tracks the final shape.
close_reason: e2e for the unverified-invitee path: banner + create-career gate (aria-disabled, keyboard-activate toast) + verify-email redirect round-trip (mints the HS256 token Better Auth never persists, drives the real endpoint, asserts ?verified=1 survived → toast → unlock). create-career is the representative gate; add-player/record-snapshot stay on component tests. Real-delivery (Mailpit) lane tracked in gf-4o8.

title: Fire the 'Email verified' toast on the fresh-land path via ?verified=1 callbackURL
description:
gf-7mm's just-verified toast fires from a sawUnverifiedRef session transition (unverified→verified), so it only shows when the user had the app open as unverified and verified in another tab, then returned (Better Auth's focus refetch flips the session). It does NOT fire on the more common path: click the email link → land on a fresh /squad page already verified (autoSignInAfterVerification). The component never observed unverified, so no toast — the user just sees the banner already gone (which is feedback, but not the confirmation the spec intended).

The original gf-7mm design (NOTES) named the ?verified=1 mechanism for exactly this case. Implement it: set CALLBACK_URL to '/squad?verified=1' in verification-banner.tsx's requestLink (and optionally the signup verification email's callbackURL), add validateSearch to the squad route to accept the param, and on load with verified=1 fire toast.success + strip the param (navigate replace). Keep the existing sawUnverifiedRef transition toast for the another-tab path, or consolidate. Discovered during gf-7mm review (spec-conformance). Low priority — banner-gone already signals success on the fresh-land path.
close_reason: Verification links (signup + resend) now redirect to /squad?verified=1 via a self-built URL in server.ts sendVerificationEmail (single source of truth, mirrors the reset flow). Squad route validates the param, fires the 'Email verified' toast once (ref-guarded), and strips it via replace navigate. Banner's now-dead callbackURL param removed. Integration test locks the callbackURL.

title: Wrong-email escape hatch: change email when typo'd at signup
description: If a user typos their email at signup, the gf-7mm verification banner shows the (wrong) address and resend can never reach them — they're stuck unverified with no self-serve fix. Add a 'wrong email? change it' path (change-email flow, re-send verification to the new address). Better Auth has changeEmail support. Discovered building gf-7mm.
notes: Backend was built then REVERTED during review (Codex P1): enabling Better Auth changeEmail let an unverified invitee escape the email-bound invite (sign up as invited@X, then /change-email to attacker@Y before verifying). Deeper issue: under email-bound invites the 'typo at signup' premise is unreachable (a mismatched signup email gets EMAIL_MISMATCH), so change-email had no legitimate caller. Whole feature — backend + UI + invite-binding design — deferred to gf-4wj. Nothing change-email remains in the tree.
close_reason: OBVIATED by the verified-only change-email design. Under email-bound invites the unverified-typo premise is unreachable (signup enforces EMAIL_MISMATCH) AND allowing unverified change-email is an invite bypass. Change-email is now verified-users-only with old-address confirmation (gf-4wj); there is no separate unverified escape hatch to build.

title: Session-bound verification-resend endpoint (ignore email param, read from session)
description: gf-7mm's banner calls authClient.sendVerificationEmail with the signed-in user's own email, but Better Auth's /send-verification-email endpoint accepts an arbitrary email param — so a direct caller can request verification emails for any unverified account (victim email-bombing), capped only by the per-IP rate limit. Close the vector entirely with a custom server endpoint (or createServerFn) that ignores client input and resends to req session user's email via auth.api.sendVerificationEmail (server-side calls bypass the public endpoint). Hardening for gf-fwi.16. Discovered building gf-7mm.
close_reason: Added a Better Auth before-hook on /send-verification-email that requires a session and overwrites the email with the session user's, ignoring the client param. Closes the arbitrary-email inbox-bombing vector at the endpoint (not just the UI call). Unauth→401. Integration tests updated: param-ignored, unauth-rejected, rate-limit still enforced.

title: Durable rate-limit storage (KV/secondary-storage) for production
description: Better Auth rate-limiting defaults to in-memory storage, which does not survive restarts or span multiple app instances — so the gf-7mm verification-send rate limit (and all BA limits) are per-instance and reset on deploy. Production wants rateLimit.storage='secondary-storage' backed by KV/Redis. Part of gf-fwi.16 production auth hardening. Discovered building gf-7mm.
notes: When implementing: Better Auth secondary-storage rate-limit keys lack TTL and grow unbounded (#4472) — use a TTL-capable store (Redis via @better-auth/redis-storage) or the DB rateLimit model, not a naive KV. The current in-memory customRules {'/send-verification-email': max 2/60s} resets on restart and doesn't span instances, so it's insufficient for the self-hosted multi-instance target (gf-fwi).

title: Collapse the repeated per-fn vi.mock factories in the module hook integration tests
description:
The gf-fwi.17 one-fn-per-file api split forced the integration tests to mock each new per-fn module separately: vi.mock paths must be static, so use-players.integration.tsx now has six near-identical factories and use-careers.integration.tsx has two, each repeating `const svc = await import('#/modules/<m>/services/<m>'); return { <fn>: ... }`. Flagged by the gf-fwi.17 review (maintainability-auditor: 'the one real regression'; pr-test-analyzer: severity-2 informational). Current form is correct and passing — this is DRY cleanup only.

Extract a tiny mock-factory helper so each vi.mock is a single line. Constraint: vi.mock is hoisted and its factory cannot close over non-hoisted bindings, so the helper itself must be vi.hoisted, e.g. `const mockApi = vi.hoisted(() => (fns) => async () => fns)` with svc/testDb also hoisted. Verify the hoisting ordering carefully (this is why it was deferred out of gf-fwi.17 rather than applied inline).

Scope: src/modules/player/hooks/use-players.integration.tsx, src/modules/career/hooks/use-careers.integration.tsx (and use-active-career.integration.tsx if the helper fits its single mock). No app changes; integration suite must stay green (9 tests across the three files).
notes:
Implemented 2026-06-18: extracted a vi.hoisted mockApi((svc) => ({ fn })) helper per file that bakes the service-import path once and threads testDb(); collapsed the 6 player + 2 career duplicated factories. use-active-career.integration.tsx left as-is (single mock, no duplication). Builder typed (svc: typeof XService) via statement-level 'import type * as' (inline typeof import() is forbidden by consistent-type-imports).

DECISION (review-cycle, user-confirmed): builder return stays Record<string, unknown>. type-design-analyzer flagged that a key typo (getPlyerFn) compiles clean; the keys-constrained alternative (Partial<Record<keyof M, unknown>> + per-call mockApi<typeof ApiModule>) needs 8 statement-level api type imports to satisfy oxlint, which undercuts the DRY goal — and a mock-key typo already fails its test loudly at runtime. code-reviewer + pr-test-analyzer agreed the conventional shape is fine. Not pursued.
close_reason: Collapsed the duplicated per-fn vi.mock factories behind a vi.hoisted mockApi helper (6 player + 2 career); single mock file left untouched. Reviewed by 4 agents (codex/code-reviewer/pr-test-analyzer/type-design): behavior byte-for-byte equivalent, integration 68 green. Record<string,unknown> return kept per user decision.

title: Subdivide src/lib by concern (logging/, utils/); move use-mounted to hooks/
description:
src/lib is a flat junk drawer mixing the logging/observability subsystem with generic utils and a hook. Group by concern — finance-aligned and consistent with ADR 0015 (refines "lib is cross-cutting infra", does not reopen it):

- lib/logging/ <- logger, is-loggable-error, request-log, request-context (+ their tests). request-log keeps its relative ./is-loggable-error import; logger keeps #/configs/secret-keys. No internal import changes.
- lib/utils/ <- number (numberOrUndefined), primitive (cx).
- src/hooks/use-mounted.ts <- moved out of lib (it is a hook; joins use-mobile).
- email/ and messages.ts stay where they are.

Repoint ~28 import sites: #/lib/logger (10), #/lib/primitive (13), #/lib/number (2), #/lib/use-mounted (2), #/lib/request-log (1), plus start.ts dynamic imports of logger/request-log/request-context. Update the architecture.md "Feature modules" / lib playbook with a one-line note that lib is organized by concern. No new ADR. No behavior change; covered by existing unit/integration tests.

Side note (NOT in this bead): primitive.ts is an odd name for a cx helper — consider renaming to cx.ts later.
acceptance_criteria: src/lib organized by concern: logging/ (logger, is-loggable-error, request-log, request-context), utils/ (number, primitive); use-mounted in src/hooks/; email/ + messages.ts stay flat. All importers repointed; architecture.md playbook notes lib-by-concern. Behavior-identical; typecheck/lint/unit/integration/build green.
notes:
CORRECTION on primitive.ts (cx): it is NOT a generic util and NOT a plain class combiner — it is the Intent-UI/React-Aria render-prop className composer (composeRenderProps + twMerge), handling className: string | (renderProps)=>string. tailwind-variants' cx/cn cannot replace it (they are plain string combiners, not render-prop-aware); keep it. The earlier "rename to cx.ts" suggestion is WITHDRAWN — cx is the misleading name; a rename should convey RAC render-prop composition (e.g. compose-render-class). Because it is a styling/RAC primitive (used only by components/ui/*), it should NOT land in lib/utils/ next to numberOrUndefined. Open question for placement: lib/styles.ts, lib/ui/, or keep it adjacent to the ui components — decide before moving primitive. The logging/ + utils/(number) + use-mounted->hooks moves are unaffected.
primitive.ts (cx) lands in lib/utils/, NOT components/ui — components/ holds only components (.tsx); a utility doesn't belong there even if all its consumers are UI components. Final: lib/ = email/, logging/, utils/(number, primitive), messages.ts; use-mounted -> hooks/.
close_reason: Subdivided src/lib by concern: lib/logging/ (logger, is-loggable-error, request-log, request-context + tests), lib/utils/ (number, primitive/cx); use-mounted -> src/hooks/; email/ + messages.ts stay flat. cx confirmed as the React-Aria render-prop className composer (kept — not replaceable by tailwind-variants; placed in lib/utils as a utility, NOT components/, which is components-only). All 11 files pure renames, ~28 importers + start.ts dynamic imports repointed, architecture.md (lib-by-concern) + styling.md (cx path) updated. Reviewed by 6 agents (all clean, 1 doc-path fix) + gates green: typecheck/lint/unit 139/integration 68/build.

title: Test getSessionFn forwards request headers to auth.api.getSession
description: src/modules/auth/api/get-session.ts (the session server fn, formerly lib/auth/functions.ts) has no test — a pre-existing gap carried through the gf-fwi.18 relocation, not introduced by it. Add a unit test asserting the handler forwards getRequest().headers into auth.api.getSession (mock both). Thin wrapper over Better Auth's getSession, so low criticality (~4/10). Source: pr-test-analyzer during gf-fwi.18 Stage A review.

title: Make forgot-password non-429 reset failures observable
description:
forgot-password onSubmitAsync swallows non-429 errors from authClient.requestPasswordReset (returns null so the user always sees "check your email") for enumeration safety. Correct for the client, but a genuine backend failure that surfaces as a non-429 auth-layer error is then invisible — no log — and the user is still told it sent.

Close the observability gap WITHOUT leaking account existence to the client: first confirm whether the request-logging middleware (src/start.ts) already captures server 5xx on the reset endpoint; if not, add a server-side log of the non-429 outcome. Client behavior (always "sent" except 429) must stay unchanged.

File: src/routes/_auth/forgot-password.tsx onSubmitAsync. Source: silent-failure-hunter during gf-fwi.18 Stage A review.

title: Migrate career/player module forms from useState to TanStack Form
description:
Per decision 0014 and the house state hierarchy (never useState for form fields), migrate the career/player module form components off useState + manual mutation + hand-rolled error UI onto useAppForm (TanStack Form). Reuse the form spine + field/error primitives established by gf-fwi.18 Stage B (useAppForm, FormTextField, SubmitButton, FormError; the AuthCard pattern where it fits).
Components: create-career-form, add-player-modal, record-snapshot-modal.
Each keeps its mutation -> invalidate flow; the form owns input + validation, Query owns the cache.
Depends on gf-fwi.18 (form primitives) and gf-fwi.8 (drizzle-zod widening normalization, so forms consume clean input shapes). Third module-alignment axis alongside the api split (gf-fwi.17) and the schema layout. No behavior change beyond added validation; covered by existing unit + e2e.
acceptance_criteria: create-career-form, add-player-modal, record-snapshot-modal use useAppForm (no useState for form fields); validation via the shared schemas; mutation->invalidate flow unchanged; typecheck/lint/unit/e2e green.

title: Move auth email templates into modules/auth/emails
description:
Follow-up to ADR 0015 and the auth-module relocation (gf-fwi.18). Move the auth-specific email templates (lib/email/templates/reset-password.tsx, verify-email.tsx) and the auth-facing rendering/sending (auth-emails) into src/modules/auth/emails/, matching the finance-tracker layout.

- Keep the generic transport (lib/email/transport.ts, transport-plan) in lib/email as cross-cutting infra.
- Repoint server.ts Better Auth hooks (sendResetPassword / sendVerification) to the module emails.
- Move co-located tests (auth-emails.test, templates.test) with their files.

Depends on gf-fwi.18 (needs src/modules/auth to exist). Deferred out of gf-fwi.18 to keep that change focused on the relocation + form dedup.
acceptance_criteria: Auth email templates + auth-facing render/send live in src/modules/auth/emails; generic transport stays in lib/email; server.ts hooks repointed; tests moved; typecheck/lint/tests/build + email preview all green.

title: Extract reusable layouts (header, footer, app shell) under components/layouts
description:
The root document (src/routes/__root.tsx RootDocument) inlines the html shell plus a global header (logo link, SignOutButton, ThemeSwitcher). There is no footer, the header renders identically on every surface (landing, auth, app), the auth pages have their own centered layout (src/routes/_auth/route.tsx), and route components each inline their own main wrapper.

WHAT: introduce src/components/layouts/ with composable layout pieces. Extract the header into layouts/header.tsx and move the SignOutButton into the header/layouts (the header is its only consumer). Add a footer (layouts/footer.tsx). Factor an app shell layout (header + main + footer) that __root composes. Consider distinct layouts for public/auth vs the gated app if the chrome should differ by context (marketing landing vs app chrome). Keep the data-hydrated marker and Providers wiring in __root.

WHY: a single home for header/footer/shell so layout changes are not scattered across __root and per-route main wrappers, and so public vs app surfaces can present different chrome.
notes: Move SignOutButton (src/components/sign-out-button.tsx + sign-out-button.test.tsx) into the header/layouts since the header is its only consumer; it already self-hides when signed out via authClient.useSession (gf-4k5). _auth/route.tsx centered auth layout is a candidate to move under layouts/. User scaffolded the empty src/components/layouts/ dir. Touches __root.tsx — coordinate with the errors bead.

title: Consolidate global error + not-found components under components/errors
description:
root-error.tsx (the RootError boundary wired as errorComponent in src/routes/__root.tsx) lives loose under src/components/, and there is no global not-found UI: __root sets errorComponent but no notFoundComponent or defaultNotFoundComponent, so a thrown notFound falls back to TanStack Router's bare default. The player detail route (src/routes/_app/players/playerId.tsx) carries a one-off inline 'Player not found.' message. is-loggable-error.ts already classifies notFound/redirect as control flow, not errors.

WHAT: move root-error.tsx + root-error.test.tsx into the new src/components/errors/ directory; add a shared not-found component there; wire a defaultNotFoundComponent (and a per-route notFoundComponent where useful) into the root route so a real global 404 UI exists; update the player route to use the shared not-found (via notFound + notFoundComponent, or the shared component) instead of the inline message. Preserve the RootError logging behavior (SSR-inline log + client effect, filtered through is-loggable-error). Import from concrete module paths per the no-barrel rule.

WHY: one home for global error/not-found UI, an actual 404 page, and no duplicated ad-hoc not-found markup.
notes: Refs: router-core/not-found-and-errors skill (notFoundComponent, defaultNotFoundComponent, notFoundMode, CatchBoundary). User scaffolded the empty src/components/errors/ dir. Touches __root.tsx (coordinate with the layouts bead, which also edits __root).

title: Validate runtime role writes from Better Auth /admin/set-role
description:
gf-utf made app-owned role reads/writes typo-safe at compile time (typed column + ADMIN_ROLE const), but the Better Auth admin plugin's runtime /admin/set-role endpoint still accepts ARBITRARY role strings — text({enum}) is TS-only and the plugin writes via its internalAdapter, bypassing drizzle's typed builder. An admin could persist a typo'd/invalid role that the bootstrap probe (eq(user.role,'admin')) would not recognize as admin. Flagged by codex (P2) during gf-utf review.

WHY DEFERRED / NOT URGENT: no consumer exists yet — there is no admin UI and nothing calls set-role, so no code path can currently persist an invalid role (the only writers are the plugin's defaultRole='user' on create and our bootstrap grant 'admin', both valid). The failure mode is also fail-SAFE (a bad role loses admin recognition, doesn't grant it; doesn't reopen the gate). 

WHAT (do this WITH the admin role-management feature, when set-role is first exposed): constrain runtime role writes — wire the admin plugin's access-control /statement model to validate role input against the allowed domain, OR add a multi-role-aware DB CHECK (NOT a plain pgEnum — the plugin stores comma-separated multi-role strings, see gf-utf). Decision 0013 currently keeps a minimal user/admin model with no granular permissions, so revisit that scope here.
notes: Source: gf-utf review (codex P2). Relevant: src/lib/auth/server.ts admin() plugin config (no roles option), src/db/schema.ts role column (text, TS-only enum).

title: Constrain the user.role column + replace the 'admin' magic string
description:
The first-admin gate (gf-fwi.2.7) rests on a stringly-typed value the schema doesn't enforce: src/db/schema.ts role is text() (nullable, unconstrained), and 'admin' is a load-bearing magic string in BOTH the adminExists() probe (eq(user.role,'admin')) and the create-hook grant (role:'admin') in src/lib/auth/server.ts. A typo in the filter would silently make adminExists() always false and REOPEN the bootstrap gate — a security-adjacent failure with no compile-time guard. Flagged independently by the type-design and maintainability reviewers during gf-fwi.2.7 review.

WHAT: constrain role to a typed domain (pgEnum or text({enum:['user','admin']}).$type<Role>()) and replace the scattered 'admin'/'user' literals with a shared const, so a typo becomes a compile error. CAVEAT: the role column is owned by the Better Auth admin plugin (defaults user/admin) — verify the typed column stays compatible with the plugin's reads/writes (it sets role on create and via setRole). Keep the gf-fwi.2.7 behavior identical; this is a type-safety refactor, no behavior change.

WHY DEFERRED FROM gf-fwi.2.7: the column is library-owned and constraining it is a separate schema/migration concern outside that bead's race-hardening scope.
notes: Source: gf-fwi.2.7 review (type-design-analyzer + maintainability-auditor). Files: src/db/schema.ts:143 (role: text()), src/lib/auth/server.ts:50,77 ('admin' literals).
close_reason: Typed the user.role column to the 'user'|'admin' domain via drizzle text({ enum: USER_ROLES }) — TS-only narrowing (verified no migration; column stays plain text so the admin plugin's comma-separated multi-role writes aren't rejected), making a typo'd role filter/grant a compile error. Extracted ADMIN_ROLE const used by the bootstrap probe + grant (src/lib/auth/server.ts); test helper insertUser tightened to UserRole|null. No behavior change (33 auth integration + 138 unit pass). Test 'admin' literals kept as test-as-spec (now typo-safe via the column type). Follow-up gf-thb: validate runtime /admin/set-role writes (no consumer yet; out of scope).

title: Enable Sentry source-map upload + release tagging
description:
gf-yru wired Sentry but deferred source-map upload + release tagging (both are the CI/deploy half of the integration). Today: stack traces in Sentry are minified, and errors aren't associated with a deploy.

1. Provision a Sentry auth token (org+project) as a CI/build secret (never committed).
2. Flip '@sentry/cli': true in pnpm-workspace allowBuilds so its binary builds.
3. Confirm the sentryTanstackStart plugin uploads source maps at build and the dashboard symbolicates client + server stacks.
4. RELEASE tagging: the plugin injects a release when uploading, OR set release explicitly in both Sentry.init (instrument.client/server) from a build var (e.g. git SHA). This closes gf-yru's one partial acceptance item ('release/environment set' — environment is set, release was deferred here).
5. Verify source maps are NOT shipped to the public client bundle (upload-then-delete, the plugin's default).
