title: Wire Sentry into the isomorphic logger + logError seam (server pinoIntegration + client captureException)
description:
gf-vy9 builds an isomorphic pino logger plus a single `logError(cause, message)` primitive that every client/server catch routes through. That primitive is the deliberate upgrade seam for Sentry — this bead plugs Sentry in with no logger rewrite.

WHY: client/SSR errors currently land in pino only (prod client logs reach the user's console with no sink). Sentry gives a real error sink + breadcrumbs/release tracking. Officially supported now, split by runtime along the SSR boundary the logger already respects.

WHAT (two runtime paths, both confirmed in research 2026-06-16):
- Server/SSR (Node): add Sentry's official `pinoIntegration` (in @sentry/node, SDK >=10.18.0, needs enableLogs) so server-side pino logs flow to Sentry automatically — no logger changes. Alt: official @sentry/pino-transport (createSentryPinoTransport) as a pino transport. GOTCHA: pino transports run in a worker thread, so the Sentry transport needs Sentry re-init inside the worker (issue getsentry/sentry-javascript#16723-class). pinoIntegration avoids the worker-thread issue.
- Browser (client): the pino<->Sentry integrations are Node-only. Add Sentry's browser SDK and call Sentry.captureException(cause) INSIDE logError — every client catch already funnels through it, so it's a one-line addition at the single chokepoint.

SCOPE: add @sentry/* deps, init server + browser SDKs (DSN via env, gitignored / deploy-secret — NEVER commit a real DSN), add enableLogs + pinoIntegration server-side, add captureException call inside logError client-side, sample-rate + release/environment config, redaction parity with the logger redact list (password/token/secret/apiKey/inviteCode/authorization/cookie — Sentry beforeSend scrub).

SOURCES: https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/node/configuration/integrations/pino/ · https://sentry.io/changelog/pino-and-consola-sdk-integrations-for-logs · https://www.npmjs.com/package/pino-sentry-transport
design:
FINAL (option B, decided 2026-06-17): capture via Sentry.captureException in the logError seam, NOT pinoIntegration. Rationale: pinoIntegration needs Sentry auto-instrumentation, which in this ESM project requires --import preload (runs before the app + before t3-env, forces raw env, fragile nitro cp step). captureException sidesteps all of that AND makes server errors first-class Sentry Issues.

CLIENT: logError gates Sentry.captureException(cause) behind import.meta.env.PROD (dev = pino console). DSN via import.meta.env.VITE_SENTRY_DSN (Vite convention, like VITE_LOG_LEVEL); unset -> Vite inlines undefined -> init DCEs to disabled. instrument.client.ts imported first in src/client.tsx; tanstackRouterBrowserTracingIntegration added in router.tsx.

SERVER: logError captureException fires server-side too (prod). instrument.server.ts is a normal BUNDLED module imported at the top of src/server.ts (no --import, no cp) -> it reads env.SENTRY_DSN + env.SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE via t3-env (validated at server boot, where secrets exist; NOT a bootstrap exception). server.ts wraps the handler with wrapFetchWithSentry (catches unhandled request errors); Sentry default integrations catch uncaught/unhandledRejection.

REDACTION: shared scrubSentryPayload (src/integrations/sentry/scrub.ts) wired as beforeSend + beforeSendLog on both inits, mirroring the logger redact list (pino browser can't redact; this is the client parity).

KNOWN GAP (acceptable): server logger.error calls NOT routed through logError (request-log, db pool, invite sweep) don't auto-forward to Sentry; wrapFetchWithSentry still captures thrown request errors. Wire them through a shared helper later if needed.

ENV VALIDATION: runtime/boot via t3-env import (server secrets are runtime-injected, so build-time validation would be wrong). @sentry/cli build script set false in pnpm-workspace allowBuilds (source-map upload deferred).
acceptance_criteria: Client: a handled error in logError reaches Sentry via captureException in prod (stripped in dev). Server: caught errors via logError AND uncaught exceptions/unhandled rejections both reach Sentry (pinoIntegration + default integrations). Switch keys on import.meta.env.PROD, not process.env.NODE_ENV. DSN sourced from env, never committed. Redact parity enforced via beforeSend. Sample rates + release/environment set. Build clean + client bundle leak grep still passes.
notes: Depends on gf-vy9 (logger + logError must exist first). Sentry intentionally OUT of scope for gf-vy9 — that bead only proves the seam. Worker-thread re-init is the one known footgun for the @sentry/pino-transport path; prefer pinoIntegration to sidestep it.
close_reason: Wired Sentry via option B: captureException in the logError seam (PROD-gated, client+server), not pinoIntegration. Added t3-env client/server split (env/{client,server}.ts) with build-enforced markers keeping server var names out of the client bundle; shared scrubSentryPayload (beforeSend+beforeSendLog) mirrors the pino redact list via a single SECRET_KEYS source of truth; server.ts wraps the entry with wrapFetchWithSentry (forwarding request opts); start.ts adds Sentry request/function middleware; router.tsx adds browser tracing; sourcemaps gated on SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN. Follow-up gf-z0b for source-map upload + release tagging.

title: Authenticated password-change flow with 'sign out other devices' option
description: Build an authenticated password-change UI (account/settings page, which doesn't exist yet) using authClient.changePassword({ currentPassword, newPassword, revokeOtherSessions }). Include a 'Sign out other devices?' checkbox driving revokeOtherSessions. This is the user-CHOICE counterpart to the forced revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset on the unauthenticated reset flow (gf-fwi.2.6 Stage 2'-b): reset force-revokes all sessions (compromise recovery), while an authenticated change lets the user decide. changePassword requires the current password, so it only applies to logged-in users.
notes: Better Auth changePassword takes currentPassword + newPassword + revokeOtherSessions (verified in better-auth 1.6 dist). Needs an account-settings surface; likely co-located with gf-7mm (verify-email resend) on that page.
close_reason: Built the authenticated change-password form: changePassword({ currentPassword, newPassword, revokeOtherSessions }) with a 'sign out other devices' checkbox (default off — the user-choice counterpart to the forced reset revoke). Wrong current password routes to the field via changePasswordFormError. Lives on the gf-4wj /account page. Browser-verified (wrong-password error + happy path).

title: Enforce email verification (requireEmailVerification on) + rework signup success/gating
description: Today requireEmailVerification is OFF (server.ts emailAndPassword), so users enter the app unverified and there is no verification UI. This bead OWNS the whole email-verification surface: (1) build the verify-email route/UX (check-your-inbox + authClient.sendVerificationEmail resend, reading the email from the client session so resend only targets the signed-in user), (2) turn requireEmailVerification ON so unverified users cannot sign in, (3) rework the success/gating flow — sign-up no longer auto-enters the app; verify-email becomes the gate; login surfaces EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED -> route to verify-email/resend (add that case to login's error mapping in src/lib/auth/errors.ts). MUST NOT lock out the bootstrap admin (the original reason the flag is off): auto-verify the first admin or provide a verified bootstrap path.
notes:
BUILT (reconciliation of design notes vs implementation, 2026-06-19):
- Just-verified toast uses a sawUnverifiedRef session-transition trigger (fires when a shown-unverified user flips to verified via Better Auth's built-in refetchOnWindowFocus), NOT the ?verified=1 callbackURL named in the design. The fresh-land case (click link -> land already-verified) shows no toast (banner-gone is the feedback) -> deferred to gf-2hf.
- Client cooldown is in-memory React state, NOT localStorage-by-email (dropped for the react-compiler set-state-in-effect rule). The server rate limit (/send-verification-email, 2/60s) is the real control.
- No custom focus-refetch effect: Better Auth's built-in refetchOnWindowFocus clears the banner on tab return.
- Gating uses a shared VerifiedGate + GatedActionButton (aria-disabled, focusable, toasts on activate). Applied to the 3 squad-write UIs that exist (create-career, add-player, record-snapshot); remove-player/invite/admin have no UI yet.
- Server-side emailVerified enforcement on mutations stays deferred to gf-fwi.3.
VERIFIED LIVE (chrome-devtools): verified-admin = no banner; unverified = banner + gated create-career button that toasts; resend -> 60s cooldown; restore-verified clears the banner. Reviewed via 2 review-cycle iterations (all converged). Follow-ups: gf-2hf, gf-3aw, gf-cpq, gf-wmc, gf-cqi.
close_reason: Progressive email verification shipped: dismissable banner (request-link + cooldown + verified toast), VerifiedGate feature-gating of the squad writes, bootstrap-admin auto-verify, and a server rate-limit on the verification-send path. requireEmailVerification stays OFF per the user-confirmed pivot. Reviewed (2 iterations), all gates green (unit 160/integration 70/e2e 8), verified live in-browser. Server-side mutation enforcement -> gf-fwi.3; 5 follow-ups filed.

title: Toast notification system (Intent UI sonner + root provider)
description: No toast/notification component exists in src/components/ui. Add Intent UI's sonner-based Toast + a provider in the root (src/providers or __root) for transient user feedback. General-purpose UI infra used app-wide: success ('Career saved', 'Player added'), info, and the prod side of the error-feedback layer (gf-vy9). title: Client error feedback: dev logger + prod toasts (hybrid with inline validation)
description: Consistent client error-feedback layer (hybrid, agreed 2026-06-16). Expected validation/credential errors stay INLINE on the form/field (already in place: FormError + field errors). Unexpected/network errors go through a reportError(cause, message) helper — dev: logger.error to console; prod: toast (needs gf-78e). Isomorphic logger: make src/lib/logger.ts browser-safe — pino browser:{asObject:true} + an isBrowser guard around the pino-pretty transport; read the client level via import.meta.env (process.env.LOG_LEVEL throws 'process is not defined' in the browser). Keep the redact list so logged causes never carry password/token/inviteCode/cookie/authorization. INFO-DISCLOSURE RULE: user-facing text (inline + toast) is curated strings WE control, keyed by error.code — never echo raw server error.message, exception text, stack, or internal codes; the raw cause goes only to the redacted logger. Nav-blocking: the catch must still return a form-level error (or mark invalid) so a network failure does not let onSubmit run and navigate.
notes: Verified 2026-06-16: invite-plugin messages are safe and login is generic/enumeration-safe, so committed Stage 2' is safe today; sign-up currently echoes error.message ?? fallback — switch to code-keyed curated strings when centralizing the error->message map. OUT OF SCOPE / optional future: global error boundary + window 'unhandledrejection' handler; server log-shipping (/api/log) with hardening (zod payload schema, size cap, rate-limit, allowlist the dynamic logger[level] lookup); PostHog/Sentry captureException (neither SDK in deps). eslint no-console blocks console.* but not logger.*(). Originated from silent-failure-hunter (LOW) in gf-fwi.2.6 Stage 2'.
close_reason: Client error-feedback layer shipped (hybrid). Isomorphic logger (pino browser:{asObject:true} + import.meta.env.SSR guard; client level via VITE_LOG_LEVEL; redact list preserved server-side, browser build can't redact so logError only takes the caught error; logError never throws). logError(cause,message) wired into the 4 auth-form catches (log + keep inline NETWORK_ERROR_MESSAGE, nav still blocked), the sign-out button (toasts SIGN_OUT_FAILED_MESSAGE on failure), and RootError (extracted to src/components/root-error.tsx; curated UNEXPECTED_ERROR_MESSAGE instead of raw error.message — INFO-DISCLOSURE fix; logs on SSR render + client effect). Browser logger is DEV-CONSOLE ergonomics only; prod client+server error sink is Sentry, deferred to gf-yru. /api/log and a logging server fn explicitly rejected. Reviewed 2 iterations; typecheck/lint/unit 95/integration 62/e2e 8/build+leak grep all green.

title: Optionally verify SMTP credentials/reachability at auth boot
description: assertEmailTransportConfigured (src/lib/email/transport.ts) validates that the email env is SHAPED correctly (CF_EMAIL_TOKEN/SMTP_URL present, EMAIL_FROM when SMTP set) and fails fast in prod when none is configured. It does NOT verify that credentials actually authenticate or the SMTP host is reachable. So a prod deploy with a wrong-but-present CF_EMAIL_TOKEN passes the boot assertion, returns 200 on first signup/reset, and only logs 'email send failed' on the swallowed per-send path (Better Auth's runInBackgroundOrAwait catches callback rejections). Options: call transporter.verify() once at startup behind the same assertion (couples boot to SMTP reachability — a blip blocks deploy, needs a decision), or document that credential validity is covered operationally via alerting on the 'email send failed' error log + a user-facing 'resend' affordance. Surfaced by the gf-fwi.2.5 review cycle (silent-failure-hunter, MEDIUM).
notes: Deferred from gf-fwi.2.5 per fix-vs-defer: needs a network call at boot and a product decision about failing the deploy on a flaky verify.

title: Establish enforced client/server module boundaries (markers + drop dynamic-import workarounds)
description:
gf-fwi.2.2 proved static import + the @tanstack/react-start/server-only marker keeps server code out of the client bundle with NO leak (verified dev AND build, auth route). Import protection is built-in/default-on (v1.168.25); markers cost nothing at runtime (virtual-emptied at build) and turn accidental cross-boundary imports into build errors. Goal: make every single-environment module explicitly marked, then collapse the dynamic-import workarounds that existed only for bundle isolation.

PART A — mark single-environment modules (defensive, no behavior change):
- server-only (import '@tanstack/react-start/server-only'): src/db/client.ts, src/configs/env.ts, src/lib/logger.ts, src/lib/request-log.ts, src/lib/request-context.ts, src/modules/*/services/*.ts. (src/lib/auth/server.ts already marked in gf-fwi.2.2.)
- client-only (import '@tanstack/react-start/client-only'): src/lib/auth/client.ts, src/integrations/next-themes/*, src/lib/analytics.tsx / src/hooks/use-analytics.ts.
- DO NOT mark isomorphic/boundary files: src/modules/*/api/*.ts (createServerFn is client-callable via RPC stub), src/db/schema.ts + drizzle-zod validators (types consumed client-side; runtime value import would break). .server.ts/.client.ts naming is an alternative to markers.

PART B — drop dynamic-import workarounds now made unnecessary by Part A's markers, and remove the matching eslint no-restricted-syntax exemptions:
- src/modules/career|catalog|player/api/*.ts (dynamic import of #/db/client + services) -> static; verify createServerFn handler stripping keeps client clean.
- src/start.ts (dynamic import of logger/request-log/request-context) -> static; createMiddleware is a different boundary than route server.handlers, test carefully.
- src/lib/email.ts (built in gf-fwi.2.4, not yet present) -> build with the marker pattern from the start; no dynamic-import exemption.

Done when: single-env modules are marked, safe dynamic imports are static, corresponding eslint.config.js ignores removed, and typecheck/lint/build + a client-bundle leak grep (.output/public) all pass. Verify BOTH dev (mock warnings) and build (post-tree-shake) per site. Recorded finding: memory tanstack-start-v1-168-static-imports-of-server. Docs: TanStack Start Import Protection.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-06-18. Part A: server-only markers on db/client.ts, lib/logging/{request-log,request-context}.ts, and the 3 modules/*/services/*.ts. Part B: dynamic->static imports in all api files + start.ts; split career/api/careers.ts -> {list-careers,create-career}.ts and player/api/players.ts -> 6 per-fn files (deleted the service() helper); catalog/api/catalog.ts kept name + static; repointed hooks + integration vi.mock paths; removed the api/, email, start.ts eslint dynamic-import exemptions.

FINDING 1 (correction to Part A list): logger.ts is NOT markable server-only — it is isomorphic by design. logError is called from client modules (use-auth-submit, use-sign-out) and root-error.tsx; import.meta.env.SSR/DEV/PROD static replacement DCEs the pino-pretty transport + process.env read from the client bundle, and pino uses its browser build. Joins authClient + next-themes/theme-provider on the 'isomorphic, leave unmarked' list. (The client-only candidates next-themes + analytics were likewise NOT marked: theme-provider is SSR-rendered via providers; analytics.tsx/use-analytics.ts do not exist yet.)

FINDING 2 (Part B start.ts, the 'test carefully' boundary): the createMiddleware static conversion IS safe. start.ts is consumed only as 'import type { startInstance }' in routeTree.gen.ts:265, so the client never evaluates it as a value module. Verified: build exit 0 (Import Protection did not deny), client-bundle leak grep shows 0 of AsyncLocalStorage/node:async_hooks/runInstrumented/runWithRequestContext/drizzle-orm/DATABASE_URL, e2e 8/8 in a real browser. Codex flagged this as a P1 a priori; refuted 3 ways. Follow-up gf-9g6 filed for the per-fn vi.mock factory duplication the split introduced.
close_reason: Implemented + reviewed: server-only markers on 6 modules, api split to one-fn-per-file with static imports, start.ts static conversion (verified clean), eslint exemptions dropped. Gates green: typecheck/lint/unit144/integration68/e2e8/build + client-bundle leak grep. Findings recorded in notes; gf-9g6 filed for vi.mock DRY.

title: Auth hardening for reverse-proxy / production deployment
description: Deferred from gf-fwi.2.2 review (Better Auth security docs). When packaging for self-host behind a reverse proxy (Coolify/Traefik): (1) advanced.ipAddress.ipAddressHeaders — set the trusted proxy IP header so rate-limiting/IP logging can't be spoofed (default reads X-Forwarded-For; Cloudflare = cf-connecting-ip); (2) advanced.trustedProxyHeaders OR dynamic baseURL { allowedHosts } if the instance is reached via multiple hosts (currently static BETTER_AUTH_URL, proxy headers ignored); (3) review trustedOrigins for prod (default trusts baseURL only — do NOT add localhost in prod); (4) consider versioned secret rotation via BETTER_AUTH_SECRETS. The wide-events design also mentioned typed context injection — next({context:{log,reqId}}) — so server-fn handlers get a typed context.log instead of the ambient getRequestLog(). Implement when a server fn actually wants the typed request logger on its context.

title: Wide-events request middleware (canonical log lines over pino)
description: Observability layer on top of the pino base logger (gf-fwi.10): emit ONE wide, structured 'canonical log line' per request instead of scattered log calls. Grounded in installed @tanstack/start-client-core 1.170 createMiddleware API.
design: Mechanism (verified against installed 1.170 source): use a REQUEST middleware — createMiddleware({type:'request'}).server(async ({request, pathname, next, handlerType, serverFnMeta}) => ...) — registered GLOBALLY via createStart({ requestMiddleware: [loggingMiddleware] }). Key facts: (1) request middleware fires for handlerType 'serverFn' AND 'router' (page/SSR), so one middleware covers both the server-fn data path and page loads — no separate Nitro hook needed for basic coverage. (2) Inputs for fields: raw web Request (method/headers/url), pathname, handlerType, serverFnMeta (fn name when a server fn). The middleware result exposes response (status). (3) Context: next({context:{log, reqId}}) injects the request-scoped pino child into server-fn context (typed via GlobalServerRequestContext); ALSO wrap next() in AsyncLocalStorage.run({log, fields}, ...) so services/db deep in the stack append fields without prop-drilling. (4) In a finally after next(), emit logger.info({reqId, handlerType, method, pathname, fn, status, durationMs, ...fields}, 'request'). (5) reqId sourcing: prefer an inbound correlation header, else generate — reqId = request.headers.get('cf-ray') ?? request.headers.get('x-request-id') ?? crypto.randomUUID(). Reusing Cloudflare's cf-ray correlates app logs with CF edge logs (the app is CF-fronted); crypto.randomUUID is zero-dep (ULID/nanoid only if time-sortable ids are later wanted). Prereq: project has NO Start instance yet (no src/start.ts) — this bead must add createStart + register the global request middleware. NOT pino-http (that's Node req/res; Start uses web Request/Response) — hand-roll with a pino child.
notes: Builds on gf-fwi.13: the Start instance + global request middleware + minimal error logging are established there; THIS bead extends that same middleware into the full wide-events model (AsyncLocalStorage field accumulation + one canonical log line per request + reqId from cf-ray/x-request-id). OWNS 5xx-response logging: gf-fwi.13 logs THROWN errors, but Start's executeMiddleware resolves returned/thrown Responses (incl. 5xx) into next()'s result rather than throwing, so they bypass gf-fwi.13's catch (codex flagged this). gf-fwi.12 logs status per request, capturing those 5xx outcomes — do it here (not gf-fwi.13) to avoid double-logging. TRIGGER to promote to a pre-prod gate (make gf-fwi.4 depend on this): once server routes (createFileRoute server handlers) that RETURN Responses exist, the 5xx-Response gap becomes real and observability is incomplete without this. Until then, the app is server-fn-only and every failure is a thrown error that gf-fwi.13 already logs, so this stays a P3 enhancement, not a deploy gate. Coverage caveat: truly raw Nitro routes outside Start bypass request middleware; negligible for this app.
